data.narrative:
Theion, a Series A climate and energy company founded by Ulrich Ehmes, is evaluated against a sector universe of 9 peers (1 public: LNZA; 8 private, including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix). The company has raised €25M+ to date.

Stage-progression valuation, the sole applicable triangulation method, anchors to the €25M raised proxy and applies a 2.0x multiplier typical of Series A-to-next-stage progression, implying a valuation of €50M. A peer-median approach was not viable: while 8 same-sector comparables exist, none satisfied narrow filters for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier valuation clustering. Employing an all-sector median would introduce unacceptable noise given the heterogeneity of climate and energy technology.

The analysis supports a range of €42M to €57M, centered on €50M median. This range reflects typical step-up variability around a single method. Key uncertainties include the absence of directly comparable Series A transactions in the narrow peer set, which limits confidence in the 2.0x multiplier's applicability to Theion's specific technology and market position. Additional data on recent Series A closings within advanced materials or energy storage would refine the step-up assumption. The valuation is provisional pending access to stronger peer anchors or internal financial metrics.
